note.text:
Predicting: when data follow a pattern, we can predict new values.
• Inside the range measured, read the value from the line (interpolation).
• Beyond the range, continue the pattern (extrapolation), carefully: the pattern may change.
A fair test changes one variable only:
• the independent variable is the one we change;
• the dependent variable is the one we measure;
• the controlled variables are kept the same.
Evaluating an experiment: Were the readings repeatable? Was the test fair? What could cause errors (reaction time with a stopwatch, reading a scale at an angle)? How could it be improved (repeat readings, use a more precise instrument, take more readings)?

worked_example.problem: A spring stretches {k} cm for every {g} g hung on it, up to {5 * g} g. Predict the stretch for {n * g} g, and say why the prediction may be wrong.
steps: {n * g} g is beyond the range measured: the spring may stop stretching evenly, so this is only a prediction.
worked_example.answer: About {n * k} cm, but the pattern may change beyond the range measured.

cards.idea: If the pattern adds the same amount each time, continue it to predict the next value.
example: {readings([a, a + d, a + 2 * d, a + 3 * d])} …: next {a + 4 * d}.

cards.idea: In a fair test, change one variable, measure one, and keep all the others the same.
example: Changed: the height of the ramp. Measured: the time.
Kept the same: the ball, the ramp length, the surface.

cards.idea: To improve an experiment: repeat readings, use more precise instruments, take more readings.
example: Timing by hand has a reaction-time error.
Repeat and find the mean to reduce it.

questions.prompt: A plant's height is measured each week: {readings([a, a + d, a + 2 * d, a + 3 * d])} cm. Predict the height next week if the pattern continues.

misconceptions.explain: {d} cm is the growth each week; add it to the last height.

questions.prompt: In an experiment on how the height of a ramp affects the time a ball takes to roll down it, sort the variables.

pool.left: the same surface on the ramp

questions.prompt: A spring stretches {k} cm with {m} g and {2 * k} cm with {2 * m} g, evenly. What is its stretch with {m + m / 2} g?
solution: The stretch is proportional: halfway between {m} g and {2 * m} g gives halfway between {k} cm and {2 * k} cm.

pick.q: Ayuk times one swing of a pendulum with a stopwatch. What is the best way to improve his result?
e: One quick reading has a large reaction-time error.
A ruler measures length, not time.
pick.y: Timing many swings makes the reaction-time error small compared with the total.

pick.q: Bih's three readings are very different from each other. What should she do?
pick.r: Repeat the measurement and check for mistakes.
e: Choosing the biggest is not fair.
pick.y: Readings that disagree must be checked and repeated.

pick.q: A pupil reads a measuring cylinder from above. What error can this cause?
e: A zero error is when an instrument does not start at zero.
Reading at an angle gives a wrong value.
pick.y: Reading at an angle gives a parallax error: read at eye level.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a fair test is wrong?

right.text: Change only one variable at a time.
Keep the controlled variables the same.
Repeat readings and take the mean.

wrong.text: Change two variables at once to save time.
wrong.explain: Then you cannot tell which change caused the result.

wrong.text: Use a different ball for each height of the ramp.
wrong.explain: The ball must stay the same: it is a controlled variable.

wrong.text: Leave out readings you do not like.
wrong.explain: Only anomalous readings, after checking, may be left out.
